messages:
jason-support: Maplify reporting increased 429s + high tail latency on Dedicated in northern-cluster. Customer says errors started ~09:12 UTC, blocking real traffic. Attaching customer logs they pasted here.
ops-bot: Created incident INC-2534021120 (priority: high) — paging oncall.
emily-sre: Pulling placement/controller logs for northern-cluster now. Seeing a surge of placement denies: reason=reserved_pool_exhausted across hostset A/B.
samir-infra: Confirming autoscaler metrics: desired_replicas=14 current_replicas=14, but available_gpu_slots=0. Autoscaler didn't trigger new nodes because metric "placement_pressure" wasn't emitted for ~8m.
adeeb-oncall: Also seeing one tenant (video-preproc-42) using ~95% GPU share on hostset-A — noisy neighbor behavior. Eviction count high on eviction loop.
jason-support: Customer repro (from their support email): curl -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/dedicated/infer -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -d '{"prompt":"test"}' => 429 with body {"error":"PLACEMENT_DENY"}
emily-sre: Repro locally against northern-cluster LB: got 429, placement controller logs: 
```
placement_controller: deny hostset=A cluster=northern-cluster reason=reserved_pool_exhausted seq=198234
response: 429 PLACEMENT_DENY
```
adeeb-oncall: Quick mitigation option: evict/limit noisy tenant on hostset-A. I can run a targeted eviction on video-preproc-42 for 30m to free GPUs. Any objections?
samir-infra: Do it. Also recommend temporarily increasing transient backfill capacity by +2 nodes while we stabilize.
adeeb-oncall: Running: `rctl tenant evict --tenant video-preproc-42 --cluster northern-cluster --duration 30m`
ops-bot: Action executed by adeeb-oncall at 09:22 UTC — eviction started. Reaction :white_check_mark: 
billing-bot: Customer Maplify impacted; auto-create credit ticket? Opening billing ticket #3456 for review.
maria-cs: Noted. I'll draft the customer message offering interim credit and explanation.
emily-sre: After eviction, placement denies dropped sharply. Started seeing placement_pressure metric again once placement-agent restarted. Found controller bug: when hostset health is reported partially, it stopped emitting placement_pressure (edge case). Repro steps for controller team attached.
samir-infra: Restarted placement-agent on host x-north-12 (09:24 UTC). New nodes provisioned at 09:28 UTC. Cluster capacity restored.
jason-support: Customer confirms success: calls are now 200s and latency back within SLO at 09:35 UTC. They still saw intermittent 429s during mitigation window.
emily-sre: Root cause summary: (1) noisy tenant overused GPU pool in hostset-A, (2) placement controller bug suppressed placement_pressure metric, preventing autoscaler from scaling out, (3) reserved_pool_exhausted logic didn't trigger cross-hostset fallback soon enough.
adeeb-oncall: Short-term mitigations applied: noisy tenant eviction, restart placement-agent, transient backfill +2 nodes. Customer notified and billing ticket opened.
maria-cs: Customer reply: appreciate quick handling; asked for postmortem and assurance this won't recur.
emily-sre: Action items: emily-sre -> open PR to ensure placement_controller always emits placement_pressure on partial failures (target: next 48h); samir-infra -> adjust autoscaler to consider reserved_pool_exhausted events for scale_up (target: 72h); ops -> add alert for >20 placement_denies/min per cluster (target: 24h); adeeb-oncall -> document eviction playbook and runbook tweak (target: 24h); maria-cs -> follow-up customer comms + credit.
samir-infra: I'll also add a per-tenant GPU cap experiment on a subset of hostsets to limit noisy neighbors.
jason-support: I'll close incident once postmortem links and customer comms are sent. Please paste PR/ticket links here.
emily-sre: Posting follow-ups: controller bug ticket #CTL-998, autoscaler task INFRA-562, alert rule PR #PR-310. Will reference in postmortem in #postmortems.
ops-bot: Incident INC-2534021120 marked RESOLVED at 09:55 UTC by jason-support.
jason-support: Resolving thread — will schedule full postmortem and share with Maplify. Thanks all for quick turnaround :heart:
